source.title: Optimization on multifractal loss landscapes explains a diverse range of geometrical and dynamical properties of deep learning

record.file_problem: The full article text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a constructed multifractal landscape and gradient descent to examine edge-of-stability behavior and how learning-rate regimes affect loss; it does not test the benchmark training-error claims or the named architectural and initialization comparisons.
record.gate_note: The VGG-16/CIFAR-10 loss-surface visualization and training-accuracy plateau are reported, but no training-classification-error result is stated. Cited results from other studies are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reproduces edge-of-stability-like dynamics on a constructed two-dimensional random landscape, not in neural-network training. Its neural-network experiments characterize landscape geometry without measuring the training dynamics or comparisons named in V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but narrower than the authors' conclusion. They propose that multifractal geometry explains edge-of-stability, chaos, and anomalous diffusion, and derive a fractional diffusion account of preferential navigation toward smoother basins containing connected, flatter minima. The claimed benefit to generalization is a theoretical interpretation rather than a direct generalization comparison in these rows.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes GD on a constructed multifractal loss landscape and characterizes its sharpness and loss dynamics; it does not reproduce the neural-network recipes in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes the loss dynamics: small rates converge slowly to a point, an intermediate broad range shows EoS and convergence in distribution, and sufficiently large rates produce excessive fluctuations. The range showing EoS broadens with the range of Hölder exponents in the landscape.

fits_no_version.finding: On the constructed multifractal landscape, terminal sharpness concentrates near 2/η over more than a decade of learning rates, while loss fluctuates locally and decreases or remains constant over longer times.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deterministic gradient descent on constructed multifractal scalar landscapes can exhibit extended edge-of-stability dynamics and convergence in distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Small learning rates converge slowly to nearby minima; extreme rates produce fluctuations preventing convergence to a low-loss solution space.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate controls the convergence regime of gradient descent on constructed multifractal landscapes.

record.peer_reviewed: Nature Communications; peer review information states that anonymous reviewers contributed.
record.problems: Core learning-rate and sharpness results are on a constructed two-dimensional landscape rather than neural-network training. Loss curves in Fig. 4c are not accompanied by numeric values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. The VGG-16/CIFAR-10 landscape characterization does not report training classification error, so it does not qualify for a row under these versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, random-label fitting, and dependence on model size, stopping, or regularization.
Spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, prevention through identity shortcuts, and training through special initialization or Fixup.
Effects of activation-matched or orthogonal initialization on training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.

All neural-network results: recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, full-batch sharpness tracking during falling loss, and divergence despite initially subthreshold rates.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization through Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied neural-network experiments demonstrate multifractal structure in two-dimensional loss sections. They do not transfer the constructed landscape's measured optimization dynamics to neural networks. No verdicts on V1–V6 follow from these rows.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large convolutional networks reach zero or near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; comparisons with smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
Whether two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks reach spurious minima, and whether extra student neurons reduce that outcome.
Whether depth without shortcuts raises training error, whether identity shortcuts prevent that, or whether special initialization or Fixup enables the stated deep-network training results.
Whether activation-matched, orthogonal, or convolutional initializations alter training speed or trainable depth in the stated networks.
The study tests gradient descent on its constructed landscape, not wide neural networks with squared loss or the full-batch neural-network sharpness measurements described in this version.
Whether batch normalization accelerates the named networks or whether Fixup matches their speed and stability without normalization.

rows.subject: GD on multifractal loss landscape L
rows.operation_detail: Varied learning rate η and initialization; tracked leading Hessian eigenvalue during GD.
rows.measure: Mean leading Hessian eigenvalue λ1 relative to stability threshold 2/η
rows.value: λ1 is at or just above 2/η over more than a decade of η values, regardless of initialization
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals shown; exact values not stated
rows.locator: Fig. 4a and Results, “Dynamics of GD optimization on the multifractal loss landscape”
rows.note: The figure plots means and confidence intervals; the text describes sharpness concentration and adaptivity.
rows.check: The sharpness result is accurately reported, but the subject is a constructed scalar landscape, not a toy neural network. It cannot establish V5's neural-network behavior.

rows.subject: GD on multifractal loss landscape L
rows.operation_detail: Varied learning rate η and measured loss along GD trajectories.

conditions.value: wide range exhibiting the EoS phenomenon

rows.value: Loss fluctuates at short timescales but decreases or remains constant at long timescales
rows.locator: Results, “Dynamics of GD optimization on the multifractal loss landscape”; Fig. 4c
rows.note: The text describes convergence in distribution across a solution space, rather than convergence to one fixed point.
rows.check: The loss dynamics concern optimization of a constructed landscape rather than neural-network training. They do not measure recovery relative to an initial linearized network's stability limit.

rows.subject: GD on multifractal loss landscape L
rows.operation_detail: Used a sufficiently small learning rate outside the EoS regime.
rows.value: Loss decreases monotonically but slowly until it plateaus at a nearby local minimum
rows.locator: Results, “Dynamics of GD optimization on the multifractal loss landscape”; Fig. 4c
rows.note: This is the study's stated low-learning-rate behavior.
rows.check: Slow convergence at a small learning rate on a constructed landscape does not measure V5. This condition would not qualify V5 even in the appropriate system: V5 does not require edge-of-stability behavior at small rates.

rows.subject: GD on multifractal loss landscape L
rows.operation_detail: Used an excessively large learning rate outside the EoS regime.

conditions.value: large enough that the distribution floods over even the largest basin

rows.value: Loss exhibits excessively large fluctuations, precluding convergence to a low-loss solution space
rows.locator: Results, “Dynamics of GD optimization on the multifractal loss landscape”; Fig. 4c
rows.note: This reports failure to reach a low-loss solution space at this extreme learning-rate regime.
rows.check: Large fluctuations preventing low-loss convergence occur on a constructed landscape. They do not establish neural-network divergence; failure at sufficiently large rates is also compatible with V5 rather than a scope limitation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
